Clients connecting to an already configured Gateway were sent through local AI-provider onboarding. That could mutate the wrong machine, expose stale credentials across endpoint changes, and start Crestodian before usable inference existed.

The Gateway is the authority for its model, agent, credentials, and runtime. Configured Gateways now go directly to the normal UI. - macOS endpoint, device-token, CLI URL, and Dashboard credentials are route-scoped and invalidated on Gateway changes.

target.title: fix(web-search): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Web search runtime config lookup paths use `"provider" in <searchObj>` to check whether a provider field is present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited property could be mistaken for an explicit user config entry.

This is the **pre-Zod validation boundary** — the raw POJO config object from `JSON.parse()` before schema validation. These `in` checks operate on the raw object where prototype-chain properties from a crafted `__proto__` survive until the `Object.hasOwn()` gate.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. Config objects are plain POJOs from JSON, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while closing the prototype-chain attack surface.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as user config entries across web search config lookup paths.

### Evidence


**Unit tests**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/web-search/runtime.test.ts` — 32 tests passed (includes 2 own-property tests)

**Runtime proof** (imported real module, tested all 4 `Object.hasOwn` code paths):

```
-- 1/5.  Core semantic proof --
  'provider' in Object.create({ provider: "brave" }):    true
  Object.hasOwn(Object.create({ provider: "brave" })):   false
  -> Object.hasOwn() rejects proto, accepts own

-- 2/5.  Loading real OpenClaw web-search module --
  Module loaded successfully

-- 3/5.  Proto-inherited provider (empty providers list) --
  resolveWebSearchProviderId(proto, []):      ""
  -> Proto-inherited provider REJECTED

-- 4/5.  Own provider selection --
  resolveWebSearchProviderId(own, [fc]):      "firecrawl"
  -> Own provider correctly SELECTED

-- 5/5.  Full tool execution --
  createTool returned:                        OK
  execute() returned:                         {"results":[{"title":"OpenClaw AI","url":"https://openclaw.ai"}]}
  -> Provider tool created and executed SUCCESSFULLY

-- CONTRACT VERIFICATION --
  in operator:         ALL proto fields detected -> WOULD OVERRIDE
  Object.hasOwn():     ALL proto fields ignored -> SAFE
  Own properties:      correctly selected -> BACKWARD COMPAT
  Execution:           firecrawl provider tool executed -> FULL FLOW OK
```

target.title: fix(ai): reject non-finite tool schema numbers
target.body:
Closes #104469

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where tool schemas containing non-finite numeric values could be projected into provider-facing schemas with those values silently changed to `null`.

The trigger is a runtime/custom tool schema that contains a JavaScript-only numeric value such as `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` or `Number.NaN` in a JSON Schema numeric constraint/default. The shared projector serialized the schema with `JSON.stringify()` before validating the projected JSON value, so those values could become explicit `null` fields while reporting no schema violation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared runtime tool schema projector now detects non-finite numbers before JSON serialization and reports the exact offending schema path as non-JSON-serializable.

This keeps the existing quarantine behavior narrow: the invalid tool is dropped with diagnostics, healthy sibling tools remain available, and provider-specific schema cleanup is left unchanged. The changed shared path is used by OpenAI and Anthropic tool projection; sibling provider paths such as Google/Gemini and Mistral use separate schema handling and are not changed by this PR.

## User Impact

Plugin/tool authors and operators get safer tool schema handling. Invalid non-finite numeric schema values now produce a clear projection violation instead of being silently rewritten into materially different provider payloads.

For example, a bad `bad_limits` tool with `maximum: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` is quarantined, while a healthy sibling `lookup` tool remains available for provider use.

## Evidence

Behavior proof:

```text
JSON.stringify({
  type: object,
  properties: {
    amount: { type: number, maximum: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY },
    score: { type: number, default: Number.NaN },
  },
})

// Before this PR, JSON serialization could turn both values into null:
// {type:object,properties:{amount:{type:number,maximum:null},score:{type:number,default:null}}}
```

Focused regression coverage added:

- `src/agents/tool-schema-projection.test.ts` covers `Number.NaN` at the shared runtime schema projection layer and expects `parameters.properties.score.default is not JSON-serializable`.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-tool-projection.test.ts` covers OpenAI tool projection quarantining a bad `maximum: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` tool while preserving a healthy sibling.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic-tool-projection.test.ts` covers Anthropic tool projection quarantining the bad original tool while preserving a healthy sibling.

Validation run:

```text

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/providers/openai-tool-projection.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-tool-schema.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic-tool-projection.test.ts src/agents/tool-schema-projection.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(agents): count CJK tool-result text by token-equivalent length
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The live per-turn tool-result truncation cap converts token budgets to character budgets with a flat 4-chars-per-token heuristic but measured tool-result text with raw UTF-16 `text.length`. A result made mostly of CJK text was accepted under the cap while its real token count was up to 4x the budget the cap exists to enforce.

**Solution**: Keep `toolResultMaxChars` as an independent **physical** UTF-16 ceiling and add a separate **token-equivalent** budget (the 30% context-share limit) measured with the existing CJK-aware `estimateStringChars` helper. The complete retained result must satisfy BOTH limits.

**What changed**: `getToolResultTextLength` stays a raw measurement (physical cap); a new `getToolResultEstimatedTextLength` measures token-equivalent length. `truncateToolResultText` gates on both budgets and re-checks the fully assembled prefix/tail/marker/suffix against the estimated budget, shrinking Unicode-safely. Plus tests and a docs note.

**What did NOT change**: The estimated budget is opt-in, so the persistence guard keeps its physical-only cap and pure ASCII behavior is byte-for-byte identical. The `maxChars` formula, the `toolResultMaxChars` config contract, and the output format are unchanged.

Fixes #103847

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `calculateMaxToolResultCharsWithCap` derives a token budget (`maxTokens * 4`) but the truncation compared/sliced against it using raw `text.length`. For CJK text (encoded at ~1 token/char, not ~1 token/4 chars) a 16000-char result reported 16000 against a 16000 cap and was never truncated, while its real cost was ~16000 tokens.

**Why This Change Was Made**: A maintainer's prior decision on this issue defined a two-budget contract — keep the configured cap as a physical UTF-16 ceiling and enforce a separate token-derived budget. This PR implements exactly that, reusing `estimateStringChars` (already used by `preemptive-compaction.ts`, `pruner.ts`, and `openai-transport-stream.ts`) rather than reinterpreting the physical config ceiling as a CJK-weighted one.

**User Impact**: CJK-heavy tool results are bounded to their real share of the context window without over-truncating results that already fit both budgets. ASCII/Latin content and the physical `toolResultMaxChars` ceiling are unaffected.

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: A tool result whose text is dense CJK (or other non-Latin) content whose raw UTF-16 length fits the physical cap but whose token-equivalent length exceeds the context-share budget.

**Root cause analysis**: The physical cap and the token budget were collapsed into one number and measured with raw `text.length`, so CJK content bypassed the token budget. A whole-input inflation ratio also cannot bound a compositionally different retained slice.

**Affected scope**: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts` — the live tool-result truncation path wired into `run.ts`, `run/attempt.ts`, and `session-tool-result-guard.ts`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Enforce a separate token-equivalent budget on the actual retained tool-result text while keeping `toolResultMaxChars` a physical UTF-16 ceiling.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node.js 22.x, OpenClaw main @ 7ac8e2e227, real exported functions driven directly via `node --import tsx` (not mocked).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Drive the real exported functions with the mixed-script counterexample and the physical-cap / live-path cases:
```bash
node --import tsx -e "
import { truncateToolResultText, truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.js';
import { estimateStringChars } from './src/utils/cjk-chars.js';
const mixed = '字'.repeat(5000) + 'a'.repeat(15000);
const r = truncateToolResultText(mixed, 1000000, { estimatedMaxChars: 16000 });
console.log('mixed retained est', estimateStringChars(r), '<=16000', estimateStringChars(r) <= 16000);
const cjk8k = [{ role: 'toolResult', content: [{ type: 'text', text: '字'.repeat(8000) }], id: 'a', timestamp: 1, toolCallId: 't' }];
console.log('8000 CJK truncatedCount', truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages(cjk8k, 50000).truncatedCount);
"
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
== P1-2 mixed-script counterexample (old code emitted ~24142) ==
input estimated: 35000
retained estimated: 15781 | <= 16000: true

== P1-1 physical cap NOT CJK-weighted: 8000 CJK, physical 16000, ctx 50000 ==
truncatedCount: 0 (0 = not over-truncated)

== live path bounds large CJK to 30% token share ==
truncatedCount: 1 | retained est: 59781 | <= E(60000): true

== ASCII unchanged ==
8000 ASCII truncatedCount: 0 (0)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The mixed-script counterexample (CJK-heavy prefix + ASCII tail) retains 15781 estimated chars — within the 16000 budget — because the actual retained text is measured, not a whole-input average. An 8000-char CJK result that fits both budgets is not truncated (physical cap is not CJK-weighted). A 30000-char CJK result is bounded to 59781 estimated chars (the 30% share of a 50K context). ASCII is unchanged.

**What was not tested**: I did not run against a real provider tokenizer (no tokenizer library is bundled); the estimate uses the codebase's own `estimateStringChars`, already relied on in four sibling paths as the corrected estimate for this undercount class.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
pnpm test -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  73 passed (73)
   Duration  5.81s
```

Adds two-budget coverage: physical/estimated separation, the mixed-script overflow counterexample, CJK Extension B surrogate safety, and live-path integration (configured-cap no-op, large-CJK share bound, mixed-script, 50K/128K tiers). Related suites pass unchanged (`session-tool-result-guard` 35, `preemptive-compaction` 22). Also validated with `pnpm tsgo:core` (clean) and oxlint (clean).

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #103847
- **Related PRs**: #104055 (competing candidate for the same issue), #103901 (earlier attempt, closed after the two-budget design was defined)
- **In scope**: Per-result live truncation two-budget enforcement in `tool-result-truncation.ts`
- **Out of scope**: The separate aggregate tool-result budget (kept on its existing raw measurement)

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — ASCII behavior is byte-for-byte identical; the physical `toolResultMaxChars` ceiling is unchanged
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 73 tests pass, config contract unchanged
- [x] No breaking changes — estimated budget is opt-in; persistence guard stays physical-only
- [x] Mitigation: reuses the already-tested shared `estimateStringChars` helper; the retained result is verified against both budgets
- [x] Documentation updated — `docs/reference/token-use.md` describes the physical ceiling plus the separate token-share guard

target.title: fix(browser): guard act hooks on current tab URL

## What Problem This Solves

`/hooks/file-chooser` and `/hooks/dialog` can trigger page-side effects, but they did not opt into the current-tab URL guard used by guarded `/act` routes. A request could arm uploads, click an upload control, or patch dialog functions while the selected tab was already on a disallowed URL.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared route helper already supports `enforceCurrentUrlAllowed`. File chooser and dialog hooks should use the same current-tab safety contract before running page-affecting hook code.

This branch also aligns the route test's `withBrowserNavigationPolicy` mock with the real helper by omitting the default `browserProxyMode: "direct"`; that keeps the focused regression test asserting the same shape production passes to the navigation guard.

## User Impact

File chooser and dialog hooks now fail closed before page side effects when the current tab URL is blocked by browser navigation policy.

## Evidence

- Enabled `enforceCurrentUrlAllowed` on both hook routes.
- Added route-level regressions proving file chooser and dialog hooks return before upload/dialog side effects on a blocked current tab.
- Focused tests/checks on head `7c93b2c6330db11c55eab2d9f717e83e4339692d`:

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as the complete canonical skill that would be applied and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without owning Skill Workshop policy

## Problem

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Design and safety

The review projection lives beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics. The service computes one canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination; channels only render portable actions.

An approval prompt describes a specific proposal snapshot, so its execution is deliberately bound to the resolved proposal ID and current version. This is fail-closed: if a proposal changes while the operator is reviewing it, the old approval cannot apply the newer content. A code-site invariant now documents this coupling. Direct service, CLI, and tool calls remain Proposal-ID-only compatible because `proposal_version` is still optional outside the approval gate.

## User impact

- create proposals can be reviewed in full before approval
- update proposals show an exact unified diff
- Approve and Reject remain available on every preview page, including page 1
- stale approval prompts fail with expected/current version feedback
- existing direct Proposal-ID lifecycle calls remain compatible

target.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Teams file consent uploads validated the SharePoint consent URL, then performed the upload PUT without a request deadline. If the upload request never completed, the accepted file delivery path could remain pending indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded consent upload timeout using the existing timer timeout resolver, and keep the abort timer active until the upload request finishes. The SSRF host/IP validation and upload headers/body semantics are unchanged.

## User Impact

When a Teams file consent upload stalls, OpenClaw now aborts the request instead of waiting forever, so the file delivery flow can fail quickly and surface the error path.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.test.ts` passed: 64 tests.

target.title: fix(signal): add timeouts to container REST requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal container REST requests already had a timeout around the fetch call, but the timer was cleared as soon as response headers arrived. A slow or hanging response body could still block REST send/status and attachment paths indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing timeout active until callers finish reading or releasing the response body. The change preserves the existing fetch helper, bounded body readers, cleanup path, and caller upload/attachment semantics.

## User Impact

If the signal-cli REST container returns headers and then stalls, OpenClaw now aborts the request during body reading instead of leaving Signal operations pending forever.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed.
